This document is mainly just to generate the new DAG based on our new list of potential counfounders, which are `AlcoholRisk`, `SmokingDuration`, `Sex`, `NonSchoolQuals`, `IncomeDecile`, `Age`, and `Waist`; the latter two being numerical while the others are categorical. As before, our main predictor is `ExerciseGuidelines` and our response is `ALT` or `GGT`.

```{r warning = F, message = F}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, 
                      fig.align='center', fig.dim=c(10, 8))

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(dagitty)
library(ggdag)
```

# Overall DAG Plot

Assuming all stated variables above are confounders, our DAG is as follows.

```{r}
# DAG Plot
dag = dagitty("
dag {
  ExerciseGuidelines -> ALTGGT

  Age -> ExerciseGuidelines
  Age -> ALTGGT

  Sex -> ExerciseGuidelines
  Sex -> ALTGGT

  Waist -> ExerciseGuidelines
  Waist -> ALTGGT
  
  AlcoholRisk -> ExerciseGuidelines
  AlcoholRisk -> ALTGGT
  
  SmokingDuration -> ExerciseGuidelines
  SmokingDuration -> ALTGGT
  
  NonSchoolQuals -> ExerciseGuidelines
  NonSchoolQuals -> ALTGGT
  NonSchoolQuals -> IncomeDecile
  
  IncomeDecile -> ExerciseGuidelines
  IncomeDecile -> ALTGGT
}
")

ggdag(dag, text_size = 1.35) + theme_dag()

adjustmentSets(
  dag,
  exposure = "ExerciseGuidelines",
  outcome = "ALTGGT"
)
```

Next, we should search for any literature that suggests that any of these variables are not actually confounders. Before, we have established that `Waist`, `Age` and `Sex` are confounders, so all that is left is to check whether `NonSchoolQuals`, `IncomeDecile`, `AlcoholRisk` and `SmokingDuration` are confounders, or some other type of variable (e.g., mediator, collider, or proxy); then, we may want to do some sensitivity analysis for those we deem other than confounder.

# Causal Inference Analysis

I believe that the other four variables should remain as confounders, which I provide more details in the `CausalInferenceSources.pdf` document. For now, I suppose we keep the DAG as is, and I also save it for future use.

Hence, we can say the following for the report.

::: callout-important
Covariates were selected based on a causal DAG informed by prior literature. Age, sex, waist circumference, smoking history, alcohol-risk level and socioeconomic position were considered potential confounders of the physical activity–liver biomarker association. Educational qualification and income decile were used as available proxies for socioeconomic position

Because the temporal relationship between physical activity and alcohol consumption is not fully established, alcohol-risk level was treated as a potential behavioural confounder; estimates should therefore be interpreted as associations with physical activity conditional on alcohol consumption.
:::
